childhood_experience: Attended St. Dominic’s School from first through eighth grade.
Volunteered with first grade and migrant children.
Taught seventh grade at St. Rose School in Longview, Washington.
Shared a birthday party with Chuck every year on the weekend between their birthdays.

Made first communion, first confession, and confirmation.

notable_stories: Signed a spelling paper for her mother in second grade and was punished for it.
Accidentally launched a pencil with a rubber band into the principal’s habit in fourth grade.
Lipsynced in choir to avoid singing and was removed for singing off key.
Fell onto Sister Angela while sliding down a railing and knocked off her headpiece.
Gave Andrew Pulaski a black eye after he kept snapping her bra straps on a crowded bus.
She says she became an encyclopedia on Abraham Lincoln and made her father take her to the Lincoln Memorial, the Smithsonian, and Gettysburg.
She reflects that she did not grow up hearing stories about her birth because her mother died when she was very young and men were not allowed in the delivery room.
Remembers the circus as her earliest memory.
Was the best bowler of her league and age group and qualified for Duckpins for Dollars.
Hated being called Babs or Babsie by her father’s family and would cringe when her aunts used it.
Hit or pinched Chuck when he called her Babs, often trying to catch him when he ran.
Beat up her brother’s friends if they called her Babs, and says Tommy Dudek was a slow learner.
Near her eleventh birthday, she shared birthday parties with Chuck because her beloved grandfather died around that time.
Remembered her grandfather as her best friend growing up and described outings with him, including Veteran’s Day poppies, doughnuts, magic tricks, poetry, piano playing, and babysitting.
Lost a Super Bowl lunch bet to Lowell Tiller and sent him a peanut butter and jelly sack lunch by way of John during a Reserve weekend.
Won a later Super Bowl bet by choosing the 49ers because she liked Joe Montana and received a catered lunch from Henry’s at St. Rose School.
Collected baseball cards from Yankees players of the 1950s and 1960s.
Remembered the Yankees as the Orioles’ nemesis and Memorial Stadium selling out when they came to town.
Remembered her dad taking the family to many Colts games at Memorial Stadium.
On the first day of first grade, she followed Chuck onto the boys’ side of the bus and then into the boys’ bathroom, which led to her being sent to the principal’s office.

She says that first-grade incident began a long pattern of visits to the principal’s office for later incidents including the pencil incident, playground incident, banister incident, confession incident, black eye incident, Brownie incident, and signature incident.
She says she and others used to steal peaches from the blind school.
She rode home from the park with her coat saturated in blood after almost bleeding to death.
She says Fred the gerbil was sucked up in the vacuum.
Spent long summer days outside until dinner time and school days outside from three o’clock until dinner.
Skated through the neighborhood after dinner while adults sat on porches.
Climbed in the quarry, climbed trees, stole peaches from the blind school, waded in streams for crawdads, and played baseball.
Once chased a flasher and threw rocks at him.
Spent Sundays at her grandmother’s house with cousins, sometimes all day and into the night.
Explored Herring Run Park with cousins.
Entered Mercy High and had to make new friends after not sharing classes with Louise and Jeanne.
Ran in a close-knit pack of friends throughout all four years of high school.
Performed in school plays including The Wizard of Oz, Alibaba And the 40 Thieves, Peter Pan, and Alice In Wonderland.
Relied mainly on the transit system to get to and from school.
Stayed friends with the same group at Towson State College.
Graduated early in December because of summer classes and married in January.
Lost touch with many of her high school friends after becoming a Navy wife.
Was a sophomore at Mercy High School when the announcement came over the intercom that President Kennedy had been shot.
Went with the whole school to the gym to say a rosary for him because the chapel was too small.
Stayed glued to the TV all weekend after Kennedy’s death.
Cried when John-John saluted his father’s casket.
Remembered visiting the state house in Annapolis because of her great uncle Teddy’s political role.
Met Brooks Robinson and Gus Triandos, and Gus Triandos signed her baseball card.
Talked to Johnny Unitas at the Golden Arm restaurant and to Alan Ameche when he came out to the car at one of his drive-ins.
Left class to investigate an unusual school announcement and unexpectedly encountered George Harrison and John Lennon in the hallway at Mercy High School.
Received detention for a week after being caught outside class during the Beatles visit, but felt it was worth it.
Saw Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel perform up close in a small auditorium at Towson State.
Was turned down by several department stores before getting an interview at Hochschild Kohn after her dad called Uncle Ted McKeldin.
Worked under the scrutiny of Mrs. Grey, who repeatedly reminded her how she got the job and seemed to wait for her to make mistakes.
Became a model employee because she felt fortunate to have the job and did not want to let Uncle Teddy down.
Grew up in Maryland and took many school field trips to major historical and civic sites.
Entered college with an open mind and initially considered veterinary medicine.
Was captivated by a Western Civilization professor who made history feel alive through vivid detail, including descriptions of Maria Antoinette and court life.
Declared History as her major because of that professor’s influence.
Completed a double major in Social Studies that included economics, psychology, political science, sociology, and geography.
Took summer classes all three years, mostly in English and science.
Became fascinated by flowers, shrubs, and trees after taking a Botany class in the summer.
Used a family vacation to Lake Chelan as part of the research for her master’s thesis on the history of Washington State.
Towed a boat around Washington for her SPU master’s class while visiting lakes and museums.
Tracked the path of the ancient Columbia River during the research trip.
Had to defend her thesis in her advisor’s office with only the advisor present and felt she got off easy.
Was raised between two brothers, many male first cousins, and boy neighbors, which taught her to stick up for herself.
Bloodied a few noses while defending herself and earned a reputation for being competitive and willful.
Had only two play dates with a girly-girl who lived two blocks away, and they did not go well.
Told her children that if they needed an instant decision, her answer would be no because she needed time to think.
Says her priorities shifted from self-development as a student to flexibility as a Navy wife and then to serving the needs of her children and grandchildren.
Says Marie took Chuck and her into her home when they were young.
Was present when Marie died on Barbara's birthday, February 12th.
Delivered a eulogy for Marie at the family luncheon after her death.
Describes Catholicism as woven into everyday life while growing up in Maryland.
Maintained church attendance through many moves during Navy life.
Made John stop in Tucson on a Sunday morning while moving from Beeville to San Diego so they could attend church.
Felt more at home with church involvement while living in Kelso.
Describes becoming more focused on Catholicism again in retirement and says she has come full circle.
Watched the assassination coverage on television.
Remembered Walter Cronkite interrupting the evening news.
Watched MLK's funeral on television.
Says the event did not affect her as deeply as JFK's assassination and funeral.
Watched the moon landing on television and found it amazing.
Followed news coverage of Neil Armstrong over the next six months.
Spent Army-Navy weekend in Philadelphia under close family chaperoning.
Was left alone with John in two connecting hotel rooms after the adults returned to Washington State, and they discussed marriage for the first time.
Went diamond shopping with John in Annapolis.
Recalls John proposing in the basement of her house.
Says they have been married 52 years and that he still makes her laugh.

Worked day shifts while John flew nights in Florida, with the two of them switching seats in the car.
Lived in unfinished housing in Beeville and helped refurbish homes while cooking on a one-burner hot plate.
Found a successful teaching approach in Meridian by using Archie Manning as a bridge topic across racial division in the classroom.
Helped form a preschool in Port Townsend and later volunteered in Brian's classroom in Gilroy.
Built a long career path through St. Rose School, Lower Columbia College, Shasta Community College, University of Portland, and Crownpoint.
Designed a movie course in Crownpoint after polling students, and it became very popular.
Resigned in Crownpoint after repeated vandalism and lack of administrative support, and later regretted ending her career that way.
Worked as a substitute for the Ridgefield School district until the pandemic shut schools down.
